info.name: School District Monitoring System API
info.description:
REST API for the School District Monitoring System.

**Base URL:** `{{baseUrl}}` (default `http://localhost:3000/api`).

**Authentication workflow**
1. Set `username` and `password` in the environment.
2. Run **Authentication → Login**. Postman's cookie jar stores the HTTP-only session cookie automatically.
3. The login request fetches `/auth/csrf`, sends `X-CSRF-Token`, then saves the rotated token from the response.
4. Every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE in this collection attaches the saved token automatically through the collection pre-request script.
5. Run **Logout** when finished. Sessions expire after 8 hours (7 days with Remember me).

**IDs**
`schoolId`, `reportId`, `userId`, and `announcementId` are captured from create responses. Run the requests in folder order the first time. `period` must use `YYYY-MM`.

**Credentials**
No credentials are stored in this collection or its environment. Use the demo accounts listed in the README, or provision your own account.

request.description: Creates an anonymous session (if needed) and returns the CSRF token. The login request refreshes this automatically, so this request is mainly a diagnostic helper.

Signs in with a username or email. Set `username` and `password` in the environment first. Postman stores the HTTP-only session cookie in its cookie jar. The CSRF token is fetched immediately before login and rotated again on success.

exec: pm.sendRequest({ url: baseUrl + '/auth/csrf', method: 'GET', header: { Accept: 'application/json' } }, (error, response) => {

request.description: Returns the signed-in user, role permissions, available districts, and the current CSRF token.

Creates an expiring reset token. The response is intentionally generic so it does not reveal whether an account exists. In non-production environments a `devResetUrl` is also returned for local testing; copy its token into the `resetToken` variable only if you intend to test Reset password.

exec: pm.test('Message does not reveal account existence', () => pm.expect(payload.data.message).to.match(/if an account matches/i));

request.description: Consumes a single-use reset token. Set `resetToken` (from a development reset URL) and `newPassword` first. Tokens expire and cannot be reused.

exec: pm.test('Reset endpoint responds without exposing internals', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 400, 410, 429]));

request.description: Six headline metrics plus the resolved reporting period. Optional query params: `districtId` (system administrators only) and `period` (YYYY-MM).
School-level enrollment data used by the enrollment chart.
Performance scores used by the performance comparison chart.
Status counts for the selected reporting period. Accepts the optional `period` query parameter.
Latest audit activity visible in the current district scope.
All districts visible to the signed-in user, each with its two PSDS assignments and school, account, and announcement counts.
School Division Office to district to school tree that powers the sidebar. Totals only count districts and schools the signed-in user can see.
Creates a district with exactly two PSDS assignments. Requires a system administrator. The code is generated from the current timestamp and the new ID is stored for the following requests.
Full record for one district. IDs outside the signed-in user district return 404 so their existence is not disclosed.
Replaces district details and both PSDS assignments. Requires a system administrator; the code from the create request is reused.
Deletes a district that has no schools, accounts, or announcements. Seeded districts with data return 409 DISTRICT_IN_USE. Requires a system administrator.
Compact list of enrolled schools used by the dashboard sidebar.
Paginated school register. Supports `search`, `type`, `status`, `reportStatus`, `sort`, `direction`, `page`, and `pageSize`.
Full record for one school. Out-of-district IDs return 404 so their existence is not disclosed.
Registers a school. A unique code is generated from the current timestamp. Requires a system administrator or district administrator. Set `districtId` in the environment (1 in the demo seed).

request.description: Archives a school without deleting it. Reports and history are retained.
Restores an archived school to active status.
Status distribution and available periods. Optional `period` query parameter.
Paginated report records. Supports `period`, `status`, `type`, and `search` filters.
Full report record, including school, period, type, status, remarks, and submitter.
Records one report per school, period, and type. Run Create school first so `schoolId` points at a fresh record. Set `period` in the environment (YYYY-MM).
Updates the submission status and review remarks for an existing report.
Paginated accounts. System administrators see every district; district administrators see only their own district and cannot see system administrators.
Provisions a staff account. Set `newUserPassword` in the environment first (minimum 10 characters with a letter and a number). The username and email are generated from the current timestamp.
Updates profile details and role assignment for an existing account.
Activates or deactivates an account. The last active system administrator cannot be deactivated.
Public list of self-registrable roles, districts, and active schools. Each role states which role must confirm the new account.

Creates a pending account. The applicant cannot sign in until the immediate superior confirms it: PSDS → district administrator, school head → PSDS, teacher/NT/adviser → school head, learner → adviser. Change the username before running this request twice; `schoolId` must belong to `districtId`.

exec: pm.sendRequest({ url: baseUrl + '/auth/csrf', method: 'GET', header: { Accept: 'application/json' } }, (error, response) => {

request.description: Lists registrations the signed-in account is allowed to confirm. Sign in as the immediate superior (for example `northhead` for a teacher) before running this request.
Confirms a pending registration. Only the role specified by the approval chain may confirm it; system administrators can confirm any registration.
Returns a pending registration with an optional reason (maximum 500 characters). The applicant is notified and cannot sign in.
Announcements visible to the signed-in role. Staff only receive published notices for their district or system-wide notices.
Publishes a district or system-wide notice. Requires a system administrator or district administrator. Leave `districtId` blank for system-wide.
Full announcement content and audience details for the notice created above.
Updates the notice title, body, or publication state.
Administrative audit trail. System administrators only; district administrators and staff receive 403.
Current user's notifications and unread count.
Marks one notification as read. Run Notifications first so a notification ID is available.
Marks every notification for the signed-in user as read.
Districts available to the signed-in account. Non-system roles only see their own district.
Updates the signed-in account's name and email. The request reuses values loaded by Current session, so it is safe to run without changing seeded data.
Installed modules, their supported actions, assignable roles, and schools. System administrators only.
Directory used by the rights page. Selects the first non-system account as the sample target for the next requests.
Effective permissions, inherited role defaults, stored overrides, and the last change for one account.
Re-saves the current matrix, so the demonstration data is not altered. A real change is a full replacement of the named modules; omitting a module falls back to its role default.
Audited permission changes for one account, newest first. System administrators only.

item.name: School forms and operations
item.description: Requires a signed-in account with learner, grades, attendance, forms, and (for health) health access. Set formsSchoolId, formsSchoolYearId, formsSectionId, and formsLearnerId in the environment. Values default to the demo seed; change them for another school. Generate SF 1 stores formSubmissionId for the PDF request and creates a new submission version in the demo database.

request.description: Returns the ten form definitions, requirements, and restricted flags.

exec: pm.test('SF 1 to SF 10 are defined', () => pm.expect(forms.map((f) => f.code)).to.eql(['sf1','sf2','sf3','sf4','sf5','sf6','sf7','sf8','sf9','sf10']));

request.description: Overview of all ten forms for one school and school year, with latest submission status and deadline.

exec: pm.test('Cards are scoped to the selected school', () => pm.expect(payload.school.id).to.eql(Number(pm.environment.get('formsSchoolId'))));

request.description: Builds the school register from saved enrollment records without creating a submission.
Creates or refreshes the SF 1 submission. Approved or finalized submissions are locked; this request stores the new submission ID for the PDF request.
Submission detail, validation issues, snapshot availability, and review status.
Authorized PDF output. The response is a PDF attachment and is not cached.
Submission history scoped to the selected school. Learner-scoped SF 9/SF 10 rows can be filtered with learnerId.

exec: pm.test('Rows belong to the selected school', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.every((row) => row.schoolId === Number(pm.environment.get('formsSchoolId')))).to.eql(true));

request.description: Daily roster. An unrecorded day returns null status, never a fabricated present mark.

exec: pm.test('No default present status', () => pm.expect(payload.learners.every((learner) => learner.status === null)).to.eql(true));

request.description: Permanent profile plus school-year enrollments used by the learner tabs.
School grading policy. A default policy is marked isDefault until the school saves its approved policy.
Aggregate-only health summary. Requires the health module; advisers and teachers receive 403.
Personnel profiles and teaching loads used by SF 7.
Submission counts, overdue requirements, validation failures, and completion by school.
Lists the signed-in teacher's assignments with quarter-level record and submission status.
Creates (or returns) the class record for one teaching assignment. Template weights come from the school configuration, never from hardcoded defaults.
Adds an assessment to a quarter. Repeat with componentKey pt and qa for performance tasks and the quarterly assessment.

exec: const saved = data.assessments.find(a => a.period === 'q1' && a.title === 'Written Work 1');

request.description: Encodes raw scores. A blank score means missing and is never stored as zero. Encode every learner before submitting; this sample uses one roster entry.
Locks the quarter and notifies the class adviser. Requires every learner and component to be complete.
Adviser-only view of the sections and subject quarters awaiting review.
Returns the submitted grades, component breakdown, and review history.
Adviser or school head returns the quarter with a reason. The teacher corrects raw scores and resubmits as a new version.
Accepts verified quarterly grades. Acceptance finalizes the matching grade_records rows and feeds SF 9.
Per-learner subject and quarter readiness for SF 9.
Lists SF 9 cards in scope with readiness, missing subject counts, status, and version.
Creates or refreshes draft cards for one section. Finalized cards are left untouched.
Returns the live or frozen snapshot, subject grades, attendance, promotion, and revision history.
Freezes an immutable snapshot and increments the version. Every offered subject must have a finalized final grade.
Reopens a finalized card with a recorded reason. The frozen version remains in revision history.
Downloads a single SF 9 PDF. The layout is a system layout, not a verified official DepEd template.
One PDF page per learner for the selected section and school year.
CSV of the register with one column group per subject. Exports follow the caller's scope.
Reads the configured components, weights, rounding, and transmutation settings.
School head or administrator saves verified weights. Never label a local configuration as official DepEd policy without a verified source.
Destroys the server session and clears the session cookie. Run this last, because every other request needs the session.
